sections.content:
The French Foreign Legion remains one of the most famous military units in the world, open to men aged 17.5 to 39.5 from virtually any country. No education or diploma is required, which makes it uniquely accessible compared to other elite forces. All nationalities are accepted as long as you carry valid identity documents.

There is one firm rule: you must apply in person at a recruitment center in France. The main options are the information office at Fort de Nogent near Paris and the preselection and selection center in Aubagne near Marseille. There is no online application process and no recruitment offices abroad, so candidates must arrange their own travel to France first.
sections.title: Who Can Join and How to Apply

sections.content:
Physical standards are straightforward but demanding. Your body mass index must be under 30, or under 25 if you aim for mountain troops. Selection itself takes place in Aubagne and lasts between 7 and 30 days depending on how far you progress.

During selection you face thorough medical examinations, psychological evaluations, and physical tests including pull-ups, the Luc Léger beep test, timed running, and swimming. Motivation interviews assess whether you can handle the Legion's famously tough discipline. Only a portion of candidates make it through to sign the initial contract.
sections.title: Selection in Aubagne: Tests and Timeline

sections.content:
The initial contract runs for five years. During basic training you are taught French from scratch, so no prior knowledge of the language is needed. A defining rite of passage is the Képi blanc march, a roughly 50-kilometer trek that earns you the Legion's iconic white kepi.

After several years of honorable service, legionnaires can apply for French nationality through a dedicated path. Note that as of 2026, Russian and Ukrainian nationals are barred from enlisting as a security measure, so check current eligibility rules before traveling.
